history.summary: THIS IS A CHRISTIAN CHURCH, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE. The Chhinga Veng Presbyterian Church serves the Chhinga Veng locality of Aizawl, near the New Market area, as a local congregation of the Mizoram Presbyterian Church Synod, Mizoram's largest Christian denomination (about 6,28,719 members in 2023), a constituent body of the Presbyterian Church of India with its headquarters at Mission Veng, Aizawl. The Synod traces its origin to 11 January 1894, when the Rev. J.H. Lorrain and Rev. F.W. Savidge arrived in the Lushai Hills (sent by the Arthington Aborigines Mission); the Welsh Calvinistic Methodist (later Presbyterian Church of Wales) mission, under Rev. D.E. Jones from 1897, took over the Aizawl field. The Synod as an organized administrative body dates to the early 20th century (1924 per the dataset brief - verify). Visitor reviews describe Chhinga Veng Presbyterian Church as a large, well-known Aizawl church with thousands attending every Sunday, near the market and easy to access. Note: the locality has several Presbyterian churches (Chhinga Veng East, Chhinga Veng South, Chhinga Vengthlang), so the CSV row may refer to the Chhinga Veng pastorate's main church (verify). Exact founding year and building history were not found in published sources (verify).

town_description: Aizawl is the capital and largest city of Mizoram, set on a ridge at about 1,132 m with the Tlawng river valley to its west and the Tuirial valley to its east. It is a predominantly Christian city where Christmas (Krismas) is the biggest festival, and churches are the centres of community life. Chhinga Veng is a central Aizawl locality near the New Market (Thakthing Bazar) area, a busy commercial zone; the church is described as being near the market and easy to access. Visitors to Mizoram need an Inner Line Permit (ILP).

travel.airport: Lengpui Airport (AJL), about 22 km from Aizawl; taxis and app cabs to Chhinga Veng.
travel.railway: Sairang Railway Station, about 17 km from Aizawl, on the new Bairabi-Sairang line (inaugurated September 2025); Bairabi station about 100 km (verify).
travel.road: Central Aizawl near the New Market area; easily reached by city bus, shared taxi or auto from the Dawrpui/Zarkawt city centre.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for cool, clear weather. Christmas and New Year are the most festive but crowded; Mizoram requires an Inner Line Permit for visitors from other Indian states.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sunday services (typically Sunday morning worship and Sunday school, with evening services; typical Aizawl Presbyterian pattern - verify, not published). One directory listing for the neighbouring Chhinga Vengthlang church gives daily 6:00 AM-8:00 PM building hours (verify, may not apply to this church). Visitors are welcome at services but should dress modestly.
